per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at five sites only: S2 < 0.70 at N53 and S292-R295 (entry 32, 268-271; PSE4-J1, r1); the rest is ordered, mean S2 0.861 ± 0.087 (J2), and the active site is the most rigid part, S2 0.88-0.97 (J3). Y105's nanosecond component is model-dependent (J4, unresolved).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window, qualitative. 32 amides need Rex from the field dependence of 15N R2 (J7, r2), most prominently T128, L221, R234, S235, G236 near the active site (J5) and R161, R178 at the Omega-loop ends (J6); S70 and A237 are broadened out (J8, unresolved) and K73 is ambiguous (J9). No Rex inside the Omega loop (J10) or at S106 (J11). No dispersion was recorded, so no kex or pB.
per_window.slower_than_ms: dynamic_in_window by NMR H/D exchange at pH 6.65 (EX2 checked at pH 7.85): I97-Q115 and N132-I137 exchange within 32 min (J12), as do E171-L177 (J13) and S235/G236 (J14); R161-N170 and most secondary structure are protected, 6-11 kcal/mol (J15, J16).
per_window.undetermined: Proposed cavity-filling Omega-loop motion (J17, homolog MD inference) and the S130 alternate side chain in the wild-type crystal (J18, abstract only, structure_only).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, qualitatively: free wild-type PSE-4 at 31.5 °C, pH 6.65 (no buffer) needs Rex terms at 32 amides from the field dependence of 15N R2, most prominently T128, L221, R234, S235 and G236 near the active site (entry 106, 199, 212, 213, 214; Rex 4.2-7.5 s-1 at 60.8 MHz 15N where given) and R161 and R178 at the Omega-loop ends (entry 139, 156), while S70 and A237 are broadened out; no dispersion was recorded, so there is no rate or population.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 6838, which the 2009 paper names as its deposition, holds T1, T2 and NOE at 500, 600 and 800 MHz (pH 6.65, 304.65 K) in entry numbering; the screen used the 500 MHz lists and flags 11 fast residues (NOE < 0.65, including N53 and S292-R295 = entry 32 and 268-271, as in the paper) and 17 possible-exchange residues (R2/R1 > 13.435), among them T128, L221, S235 and G236 (entry 106, 199, 213, 214). R234 (entry 212) is not flagged, which fits the authors' report that its 500 MHz R2 is lowered by overlap with K192.
open_conflicts: K73: highest-ranked model has no Rex and S2 0.94, against a weak amide peak and side-chain signals lost beyond C-gamma (J9, r2).

Omega loop: Rex only at the hinges R161/R178 and none inside (J6, J10), fast H/D exchange at E171-L177 (J13) but protection at R161-N170 (J15); the authors reconcile these with a proposed cavity-filling motion that rests on TEM-1 MD (J17).
Y105: two-timescale versus single-timescale model fit almost equally (J4, r1).
Author label 'R161-E170' versus N170 in the sequence (r3); mapped here as R161-N170.
questions_for_gina: Should the RelaxDB 6838 label at R234 (entry 212) be read against the 600 MHz data, given the 500 MHz R2 overlap with K192 that the authors report?
Should the qualitative two-field Rex (no CPMG) count as us-ms evidence for the WT apo answer, or only as indirect support?
protein_summary.buffer_note: No buffer was used: phosphate was omitted because it binds the TEM-1 active site weakly, DSS was used only externally, and no protease inhibitors were added because some bind the active site; the sample holds 3 mM imidazole and 0.1% azide at pH 6.65, 31.5 °C. The 81.0 MHz R2 data were excluded for inconsistency, so Rex rests on 50.6 and 60.8 MHz R2 and is reported scaled to 60.8 MHz. H/D exchange used lyophilized protein dissolved in D2O; the pH 7.85 control used a room-temperature probe. The full S2, Rex and exchange tables (SI Tables S2-S4) were unavailable.
